name: Universal Ω Nucleus Contract
$comment: THE Ω Nucleus completeness contract. A Nucleus is the complete constitutional universe of exactly one canonical concept; this document declares WHICH facets that completeness consists of and, for each, the ONE evidence that discharges it. The contract is generic by construction: it names no domain, no capability, no package and no project. It is satisfiable by unlimited future nuclei because every facet resolves against the nucleus's own declaration, against a constitutional gate the nucleus already passes, or against the nucleus's declared profile — never against a list of known nuclei. Adding a facet is an entry here and requires NO change to nucleus.py; registering a nucleus is an entry in the capability register and requires no change to either.
$posture_comment: This contract EXTENDS the existing capability register rather than establishing a second one. UFC-14 forbids two implementations of one constitutional model, and 'what is the atomic unit of canonical ownership' is one model. The register is therefore the Ω Nucleus registry, and this document is the completeness profile attached to every entry in it — exactly the 'profile over the existing registry substrate, not a new store' the Nucleus constitutional model requires.
$resolution_comment: Three resolution kinds, and deliberately no fourth. DECLARATION resolves a named field of the nucleus declaration and requires it to be non-empty. GATE resolves a constitutional gate and requires that gate to have PASSED for this nucleus, so a facet already proven by the Constitution is never proven a second, weaker way. PROFILE resolves a dotted path in the nucleus's declared profile block, whose leaf SHALL state a status of 'present' with evidence or 'not-applicable' with a rationale. A leaf that states neither is MISSING: an unstated facet is never read as absent-by-intent, because 'nobody wrote it down' and 'it does not apply' are different facts and only one of them is a determination.

facets.name: identity
facets.rationale: The nucleus names the symbol that carries its own identity, so identity is self-declared rather than assigned by a governor.

facets.name: universal-identifier
facets.rationale: The one identifier under which the nucleus is registered, referenced and composed. Distinct from NF-01: NF-01 is where the identity lives, NF-02 is the identity itself.

facets.name: canonical-ownership
facets.rationale: Exactly one canonical owner per concept. The nucleus declares who owns it and on what evidence, so ownership is never inferred from location.

facets.name: repository-truth-binding
facets.rationale: Which class of Repository Truth the nucleus's own artifacts occupy. A nucleus that cannot say whether its outputs are Truth cannot be replayed against Truth.

facets.name: constitutional-registration
facets.rationale: Registration is proven by the identity being self-declared and absent from every governing module — that is what makes a nucleus registrable without editing the governor.

facets.name: discovery
facets.rationale: A nucleus is discoverable because it publishes a descriptor, not because a catalogue happens to mention it.

facets.name: dependency-declaration
facets.rationale: Every declared dependency resolves to a registered nucleus and is really imported. A nucleus with no dependency discharges this too: zero declared dependencies is a determination, not an omission.

facets.name: capability-declaration
facets.rationale: What the nucleus offers is its published contract surface. A capability claimed anywhere else is unbindable.

facets.name: context-declaration
facets.rationale: The contexts in which the nucleus holds — and, more importantly, the contexts it does not assume. This is where a finite assumption would have to be written down, which is what makes its absence checkable.

facets.name: configuration
facets.rationale: Behaviour is configured by a declared document that resolves and parses, or the nucleus is declared policy-free. Configuration by code is not configuration.

facets.name: composition
facets.rationale: How the nucleus enters a larger composition, and what role it plays there. Distinct from NF-07: NF-07 proves the graph is closed, NF-11 declares the composition posture.

facets.name: runtime-integration
facets.rationale: The nucleus registers into the certified service registry, that registry validates, and the service resolves to a live instance.

facets.name: api-generation
facets.rationale: Which programmatic surface is derived from the declaration rather than hand-written. A hand-written API is a maintenance obligation the Foundation exists to remove.

facets.name: cli-generation
facets.rationale: The nucleus is operable in one command through a declared entry point that the build really publishes.

facets.name: documentation-generation
facets.rationale: Documentation derived from the declaration cannot drift from it. Documentation authored beside the declaration always can.

facets.name: test-generation
facets.rationale: Which tests are derived from the contract. Declaring this is what stops a generated artifact from arriving with no executable obligation attached.

facets.name: validation
facets.rationale: Every population the nucleus holds is ordered by declared precedence, refuses a conflicting redefinition, and reports an unknown member rather than substituting a default.

facets.name: verification
facets.rationale: The nucleus comes into existence through a declared bootstrap and performs no import-time side effect, which is the property that makes independent verification possible at all.

facets.name: certification
facets.rationale: Two independent builds are byte-identical and content-addressed, and a nucleus whose outputs become Truth carries a replay target. Certification pins a fingerprint, never a claim.

facets.name: monitoring
facets.rationale: What is watched while the nucleus runs, and by whom. A nucleus nobody watches is a nucleus nobody can operate.

facets.name: measurement
facets.rationale: Which registered policy measures this nucleus. One subject population yields one measurement, so the measuring authority must be named rather than assumed.

facets.name: observability
facets.rationale: The signals the nucleus emits about itself. Distinct from NF-20: NF-22 is what the nucleus makes visible, NF-20 is what a watcher does with it.

facets.name: traceability
facets.rationale: The path from the nucleus back to the authority that admitted it. An untraceable nucleus cannot be governed after the fact.

facets.name: evidence
facets.rationale: What the nucleus produces that a later determination can rely on, and where it is recoverable from.

facets.name: versioning
facets.rationale: One declared semantic version governs the whole published surface, and the version the nucleus declares is the version its contract carries.

facets.name: evolution
facets.rationale: How the nucleus changes without breaking its consumers. Declaring the evolution posture is what makes 'additive' auditable instead of aspirational.

facets.name: governance
facets.rationale: Absent, ambiguous or malformed input is refused through typed errors carrying distinct stable codes. A nucleus that guesses is a nucleus that cannot be governed.

facets.name: security
facets.rationale: The trust boundary the nucleus sits on and the authority it requires. A nucleus that never states its boundary is assumed to have none, which is the assumption that ends badly.

facets.name: compliance
facets.rationale: The obligations the nucleus is held to beyond this Constitution, or the declared determination that there are none.

facets.name: commercialization
facets.rationale: Whether the nucleus is offered as a product in its own right. Declared once, at the nucleus, so no downstream catalogue has to guess.

facets.name: billing
facets.rationale: The metering posture. A nucleus that is not metered SHALL say so, because an unstated meter is the one that gets invented later by whoever needs a number.

facets.name: licensing
facets.rationale: The terms under which the nucleus may be used and redistributed.

facets.name: marketplace
facets.rationale: Whether the nucleus is independently listable, and under what identity. Listability is a property of the nucleus, never of a catalogue that discovers it.

facets.name: extensibility
facets.rationale: New authority enters through a declared extension point, so admitting an authority never requires editing the nucleus that consumes it.

facets.name: specialization
facets.rationale: No module of the nucleus carries a project locator, so a project-specific fix has nowhere to be written and specialisation stays a declaration.

facets.name: contract-surface
facets.rationale: A consumer binds to a named, semantically versioned contract and never to a module. Distinct from NF-08: NF-08 declares where the surface is, NF-36 proves it is published.
